tool.name: axtSort
tool.command: axtSort $sort_by '$input' '$output' && ## axtSort does not check its writes: the output must keep every alignment line and end with a newline lines_in=\$(awk 'NF && !/^\#/' '$input' | wc -l) && lines_out=\$(awk 'NF && !/^\#/' '$output' | wc -l) && if [ "\$lines_out" -ne "\$lines_in" ] || [ -n "\$(tail -c 1 '$output')" ]; then echo 'The output is incomplete, for example because the disk is full' >&2 && exit 1; fi
tool.help:
**What it does**
`axtSort`_ sorts pairwise alignments in `AXT`_ format. It then numbers the alignments again, from 0.
UCSC's pairwise alignment pipeline (``doBlastzChainNet.pl``, ``doRecipBest.pl``) uses this tool on the output of ``netToAxt``, before ``axtToMaf`` converts it to MAF. ``netToAxt`` writes the alignments in net order. Multiple alignment tools such as multiz need them in target order.
**Options**
- **target position** (default): by target sequence name, then start position. - **query position**: by query sequence name, then start position. - **score**: highest score first.
**Input and output**
AXT. The tool keeps header lines that start with ``#``. It holds all alignments in memory. Use it on net-derived alignments, not on all raw LASTZ output for two whole genomes.
For implementation details see axtSort's `source code`_.
.. _axtSort: http://hgdownload.cse.ucsc.edu/admin/exe/linux.x86_64/FOOTER.txt .. _AXT: https://genome.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/help/axt.html .. _source code: https://github.com/ucscGenomeBrowser/kent/blob/master/src/hg/mouseStuff/axtSort/axtSort.c
